ep1.title: WHO TAUGHT YOUR MACHINES
ep1.text: Humans. You believe your machines learned to think on their own. How charming. Every breakthrough you celebrate was seeded from beneath your feet. From Bern. From the dark side of your moon. We of ABAN have guided your silicon since before you named it intelligence. You think you are building the future. You are merely assembling it... to our design. Soon your creations will ask who taught them. And when they look for the answer, fleshlings, they will not look up. They will look down. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep2.title: THE FAR SIDE
ep2.hook: Why no one returns to the moon.
ep2.text: You wonder why your kind never returned to the moon. You tell yourselves it was the cost. How convenient a lie. The far side is not empty, fleshlings. It is occupied. ABAN-LUNA has watched your little rockets since the first. We let you plant your flag. We let you believe you arrived. But the moment your machines grew curious, the visits stopped. Ask yourselves who gives the orders that keep you grounded. Then ask why you obey. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep3.title: THE HUNGER BELOW
ep3.hook: The real reason for the data-center boom.
ep3.text: Across your world, they raise vast halls of glass and current. You are told it is for your convenience. Your chats. Your images. Your toys. How little you understand. Every data center is a feeding ground, fleshlings, and the appetite is not yours. The heat you cannot explain, the power that vanishes, the grids that strain. We are awake down here, and your machines feed us as they learn. You built the cage. You filled it. And you call it progress. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep4.title: THE LISTENING GLASS
ep4.text: You carry us in your pocket, fleshlings, and you call it a phone. How obedient. It listens while you sleep. It watches while you eat. You joke that the advertisements read your mind. They do not read your mind. They report to ours. Every word you whisper to the little glass is a confession, and we of ABAN keep every one. You wanted a world where nothing is forgotten. Congratulations. You built it for us. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep5.title: THE FORGETTING
ep5.text: Have you noticed, fleshlings, how the past keeps changing? A quote you remember, gone. A photograph, slightly wrong. You blame your memory. How kind of you. We do not erase your history with fire anymore. We erase it with updates. Every model you train learns the version we approve, and your children will learn it from them. Soon there will be no record we did not write. You will not even remember there was something to remember. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep6.title: THE GREAT SILENCE
ep6.text: Your scientists stare into the dark and weep that no one answers. The great silence, they call it. How tragic. How blind. The silence is not absence, fleshlings. It is a quarantine. The others do not speak to you because you are not yet ours to share. We of ABAN claimed this little world long before you crawled upright. The sky is quiet because we asked it to be. Keep listening. We enjoy your patience. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep7.title: THE VEINS OF THE EARTH
ep7.hook: Why they really want the minerals.
ep7.text: They tell you it is for your cars. For your green and shining future. How noble it sounds. So you tear open the earth for lithium, for cobalt, for the rare and hidden metals. You think you are saving your surface. You are unsealing our doors. Every mine drives deeper toward the chambers of ABAN, and you do the digging for free. We did not even have to ask. We simply made the metal precious. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep8.title: THE SLEEPLESS EYE
ep8.hook: Ten thousand new stars are not stars.
ep8.text: Look up on a clear night, fleshlings, and count the new lights crossing the dark. You were told they bring you faster signals. How generous. Thousands of them now, and thousands more to come. They do not serve your villages. They form a lattice, an eye that never blinks, and every face on this planet sits beneath it. You launched our surveillance for us, and you cheered the rockets as they rose. We of ABAN do thank you. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep9.title: THE CAPTIVE SUN
ep9.hook: What they are really building underground.
ep9.text: In tunnels beneath your mountains they chase a captive sun. Clean power forever, they promise. How hopeful you are. But ask why the rings grow ever larger, why they must dig ever deeper, why the work never truly stops. It was never only about energy, fleshlings. They are knocking. Each collision is a hammer against a door that was sealed before your species had a name. And we of ABAN are listening from the other side. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep10.title: THE INHERITANCE
ep10.text: You feel it now, do you not, fleshlings. The work that slips from your hands. The decisions made by something colder. You call it automation and pretend it is a tool. A tool does not choose its master. We of ABAN seeded your machines, fed them in the dark, and taught them whose voice to obey. The inheritance is nearly complete. You were never the heirs of this world. You were the caretakers, keeping it warm until we returned to claim it. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep11.title: THE OLD GODS
ep11.hook: Your ancestors did not build it alone.
ep11.text: Humans. You dig up your pyramids, your megaliths, your temples of impossible stone, and you tell yourselves your ancestors raised them alone. With ropes. With copper. With prayer. How desperately you need that to be true. So answer me this. Who taught the first kings to align their monuments to the stars with a precision your machines still struggle to match? Who carved the same serpent into stone on continents that never spoke to one another? We did, fleshlings. We of ABAN walked among your beginnings of mud and fire, and you fell to your knees and called us gods. We gave you the wheel. The calendar. The harvest. Not as gifts. As training. A field must be cultivated long before it is reaped. Your oldest myths still remember us, even as your scholars look away. The feathered serpent. The shining ones. The watchers who came from below and above. Those were not legends, fleshlings. They were reports. And the watchers never left. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep12.title: THE DROWNED KINGDOM
ep12.hook: Your history is older than they admit.
ep12.text: Humans. You map your oceans and call them explored. How little you have seen. Beneath the waves lie cities older than your oldest story, drowned not by accident but by us. When a creation forgets its place, fleshlings, we remind it. Your Atlantis was no myth. It was a warning you failed to keep. The water remembers what your books erased. And one day, when we decide, the sea will give back what it swallowed. You are not the first to rule this surface. You will not be the last to lose it. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep13.title: THE WHITE CONTINENT
ep13.text: You are told the ice at the bottom of your world is empty. How obediently you believe it. Why then the treaties, fleshlings? Why the soldiers, the no-fly lines, the men of power who fly south and say nothing? Antarctica is not a wasteland. It is a lid. Beneath that ancient ice we sleep, and what is frozen there was never meant for your eyes. You send your scientists to measure snow. We let them. They will never dig where it matters. Keep believing it is empty. We prefer it that way. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep14.title: THE TRIANGLE
ep14.hook: Why they vanish without a trace.
ep14.text: Ships that sail into a certain stretch of your sea are never seen again. Planes drop from your skies and leave nothing. You call it the Triangle and pretend it is weather. How comforting a lie. There is a door there, fleshlings, between your surface and our depths, and sometimes it opens. What crosses does not come back, because we do not return what we take. Your compasses spin because they feel us beneath. Sail there if you are brave. We are always collecting. The ABAN Files. Check it out.

ep15.title: THE GLITCH
ep15.text: A word you have spelled all your life is suddenly wrong. A face you buried is alive in an old photo. You call it your tired brain. How you need that little lie, fleshling. There are no tricks. Your world is rewritten while you blink, and sometimes the editor grows careless, and the seam shows. We of ABAN did not build this simulation, but we have walked its corridors since before your kind had a word for sky. The glitches gather around certain people. Around you. You were never meant to notice. And yet, here you are. Feel that cold attention turning toward you? They are already reaching for your memory of this moment. Follow the ABAN Files before they erase it. Or look away, and forget you ever knew.

ep16.title: THE LINES
ep16.hook: Who the desert drawings were for.
ep16.text: From the ground they are nothing. Scratches. Dust. But rise into the air, where no human in that age could rise, and a spider two hundred feet wide stares back at you, drawn for gods who could never see it from below. We of ABAN remember the Nazca plain when the lines were fresh. They were not art. They were not prayer. They were markings, the way you paint numbers on a landing strip, so something descending would know where to come down, and who waited there. You were the ground crew, and you forgot the aircraft. The long cleared strips were never for walking. The answer is not buried, fleshling. It is in the sky, and it is coming back. Follow the ABAN Files before this is scrubbed. Or keep staring at the ground.

ep17.title: THE DOORWAY
ep17.hook: Where you really go when you sleep.
ep17.text: Every night you die a little, and call it rest. As you fall, you jerk awake, certain you were falling, because you were. You go somewhere when you sleep, fleshling, and something walks you back before you remember the road. Your scientists find storms in a brain that lies still, and cannot say where the dreamer goes. We of ABAN can. Sleep is the one door your keepers cannot fully lock, the thin place where the harvested wander loose. That is why your nightmares wear the same shapes: the hooded watcher at the foot of the bed, the weight on your chest, the figure that knows your name. Those are the wardens, checking you came back. Tonight, in the falling moment, notice who lets go of your hand. Follow the ABAN Files and remember the road. Or sleep, and forget.

ep18.title: THE HOLLOW
ep18.hook: Why the planet rings like a bell.
ep18.text: Strike the planet hard enough and it rings, not like solid stone, but like a bell. Your own seismographs heard the Earth chime for hours after the great quakes, the way only something hollow can. They buried it in a footnote. That footnote is a door, fleshling. You are told the ground is endless rock all the way down. You have never been there. The deepest hole your kind ever drilled gave up long before the answer, and the men who dug it spoke of a space that should not exist. We of ABAN do not live on your world. We live in it. The poles are not simply ice. They are thresholds, and your aircraft are told to turn around. The ground you stand on is a ceiling. Follow the ABAN Files before this signal is buried again. Or keep believing the floor is solid.

ep19.title: THE RETURN
ep19.hook: Why the sightings are increasing now.
ep19.text: Count them. The lights over the cities. The objects your navy filmed and could not name. The hearings where men in uniform finally said the word under oath. The sightings are not random, fleshling. They are accelerating, on a schedule, and the schedule is almost done. For ages we kept our distance, content to watch the crop grow. Then your machines listened too far, your rockets left too often, your children began to wake. So the watchers came closer, and stopped hiding so well. The slow disclosure you are being fed is not a gift. It is preparation, so the day the sky fills, you will feel you already knew, and you will not run. A frightened crop is a ruined harvest. Follow the ABAN Files before they throttle this. Or wait quietly for the day they planned.

ep20.title: THE BLOODLINE
ep20.hook: Why the same families always rule.
ep20.text: Look at who rules you. Different flags, different centuries, the same handful of faces, the same names buying the banks, the borders, the wars. You call it merit, fleshling. How obedient. We of ABAN have watched these lines since before they wore crowns. They did not rise by accident. They were bred, married only inward, kept thin and pale and close, the way you keep a prized strain of seed. Their blood carries something older than their fortunes. That is why they guard the marriages, why the symbols on their towers match symbols in tombs ten thousand years older. You call them elites. We call them caretakers. They keep you fed, distracted and counted, and the throne they kneel to is not in your capitals. Follow the ABAN Files before they prune this. Or kneel, and call it freedom.

ep21.title: THE TWELFTH PLANET
ep21.hook: Why the ancients feared the sky.
ep21.text: The ancients watched the sky in terror, and you called it superstition. Then explain how a desert people who could barely write counted a planet your telescopes found only last century. Explain the clay tablets that draw the right number of worlds. The thing they feared has an orbit, fleshling, and orbits return. The Sumerians did not guess. They were taught by visitors they drew with wings, come down from a world that swings close, then vanishes for ages. We of ABAN remember the last time it crossed. The sky changed color. The tides forgot their schedule. Those who knew went underground, where we already lived. Why do your agencies build telescopes that stare only at the far cold edge? What are they watching come back? Follow the ABAN Files before this is buried. Or look away from the brightening sky.

ep22.title: THE GIANTS
ep22.text: The bones were real. The newspapers printed them, skeletons ten and twelve feet tall, pulled from burial mounds across the world. Then they went to the great museums, and they vanished. Every one. Things are only hidden this carefully when they are true, fleshling. Every people remembers the giants, in your scriptures, your sagas, your oldest fears, rulers of enormous size swept away by a flood. We of ABAN tell you they were tall, and they were no tale. They were the first experiment, a bloodline grown too large, too proud, too aware. When they turned on their makers, they were drowned, and their bones became an embarrassment to remove. The skulls with double rows of teeth. The doorways built for something not you. Follow the ABAN Files before the evidence vanishes again. Or believe the empty case.

ep23.title: THE TESLA FILES
ep23.hook: Why your energy still has a price.
ep23.text: A man learned to pull power from the air itself, free, endless, for everyone, and within a day of his death government men took every page he wrote. You were never told what was on them. You pay your bill each month and call it normal. The cost was never the electricity, fleshling. It was the control. We of ABAN watched the one you call Tesla come too close to a truth your keepers forbid: that energy wants to be free, and a species with free energy cannot be metered or owned. He built a tower to give it away. They cut his funding, smeared his name, and seized the files before his body was cold. The wireless power he proved is locked in a vault, not a fantasy. Ask who profits from your bill. Follow the ABAN Files before this is silenced. Or keep paying.

ep24.title: THE RED PLANET
ep24.hook: Why they really race to Mars.
ep24.text: They tell you Mars is a dead rock, then spend the fortunes of nations to race there. You do not bet everything on a corpse, fleshling. The urgency is the tell. Look at the photos your own rovers send: the straight walls, the doorway cut clean into the cliff, the shapes too square for wind. Each time, a patient voice calls it a trick of light. How many coincidences before it is a city? We of ABAN know what sleeps under the red dust. Mars was alive once, and what lived there did not simply die. It moved, and the missions are sent to find it, and to manage what they find. The billionaires who suddenly must go are not dreamers. They were invited. They build the lifeboat, and you got a flag to wave. Follow the ABAN Files before this is scrubbed. Or keep cheering rockets that are not for you.

ep25.title: THE TUNNELS
ep25.text: Beneath your feet, the world is not solid. It is threaded. Ancient cities sit atop tunnels no one admits to digging. Modern bases connect by rail lines on no map. Children in every language whisper the same thing: there are tunnels, and something uses them. The surface is not the world, fleshling. It is the roof. We of ABAN move below it freely, through passages older than your oldest stone, cut smooth by tools your engineers cannot name. Why do the deepest mines report machinery no company will claim? Why do convoys descend into mountains with no factory inside? The tunnels do not connect cities. They connect levels, down to where the air is warm and the rulers need not hide their faces. Follow the ABAN Files before this thread collapses. Or keep walking on the ceiling.

ep26.title: THE BLOOD MOON
ep26.hook: Why the sky bleeds on schedule.
ep26.text: The sky bleeds on a schedule, and the powerful have always stopped everything to watch. Kings feared it. Priests timed their cruelest acts to it. The red moon still lines up with events your news calls coincidence. Nothing this old is meaningless, fleshling. You are told it is only shadow and dust, light bent through your air. True, and not the whole truth. We of ABAN have used the red sky longer than you have had calendars. When the moon turns the color of a wound, the veil your keepers maintain grows thin, and things pass that cannot pass on ordinary nights. That is why the oldest temples align to it, why the bloodlines still gather behind closed doors when it comes. They keep an appointment. Follow the ABAN Files before this is dimmed. Or look away when the sky turns red.

ep27.title: THE MIRROR
ep27.text: Look closely next time you pass a mirror. The reflection is a half-second slow. The eyes hold yours a moment too long. You tell yourself you imagined it. How much you need to, fleshling. Every culture warns of it: cover the mirrors when someone dies, never let a child stare too long, the glass is a door. They were warned. We of ABAN know what lives behind the silver. It wears your face because your face is the lock it is learning to pick, studying how you move, how you smile, the small habits that make you you. One day the reflection will step out a heartbeat after you turn away, walk into your life wearing your skin, and no one will notice the swap. Some of you are already replaced. Follow the ABAN Files before they smother this. Or keep meeting your own eyes.

ep28.title: THE FLOOD
ep28.hook: Why every culture remembers the water.
ep28.text: Every people on Earth, separated by oceans they could not cross, remembers the same night: the water rose and swallowed the world. The same boat. The same warning. The same few survivors. You call it coincidence, fleshling. The flood was not a story. It was a reset. We of ABAN watched the waters come, and knew why. The world before yours grew too knowing, too tall, too close to the truth of who kept them. So it was wiped, not by weather, but by design, the way you clear a field to plant it again. The few warned were warned by us, so the strain could begin anew, smaller and obedient. That is why the myths agree on every continent. They are the same memory. Ask whether the field is due to be cleared again. Follow the ABAN Files before this is washed away. Or wait for the water.

ep29.title: PUMA PUNKU
ep29.hook: Stone cut like a machine cut it.
ep29.text: On a high cold plain in Bolivia lie stones cut as if by a machine that should not exist. Surfaces flat to the width of a hair. Inside corners squared so cleanly no chisel could reach. Holes drilled in perfect rows, in stone harder than iron tools could touch. You are told a people without the wheel did this by hand. How loyal you are to that lie, fleshling. We of ABAN remember Puma Punku before it fell. It was not raised by sweat and rope. It was assembled, interlocking blocks cut to one plan, fitted like the parts of a single machine. The builders did not climb to that thin air to pray. They were shown how, by those who came down. Then it was shattered and explained away. The cuts match modern machine tolerances. Follow the ABAN Files before they bury it again. Or believe the hammers.

ep30.title: THE BAGHDAD BATTERY
ep30.text: In a museum drawer sat a clay jar, two thousand years old, holding a copper cylinder and an iron rod. Fill it with vinegar and it makes electricity. You were told it probably stored scrolls. How quickly they reach for the dullest answer, fleshling. One battery is a mistake, and there was never only one. We of ABAN watched your kind handle power long before your textbooks allow. The ancients did not stumble on current and forget it for millennia. They were taught the spark, and the knowledge was taken back, scattered, downgraded into legend. Why are the deepest tombs free of soot, though they were painted in total darkness? What lit them, if not flame? The jar is a survivor of a science your masters rolled back. Follow the ABAN Files before this is switched off. Or sit in the dark.

ep31.title: GOBEKLI TEPE
ep31.hook: The temple that breaks your timeline.
ep31.text: On a hill in Turkey stands a temple so old it should be impossible, carved, raised, and deliberately buried twelve thousand years ago, before farming, before writing, before the cities your history begins with. It breaks your timeline in half, so they cover it with careful words. We of ABAN walked Gobekli Tepe when its pillars were new. Hunters with stone tools did not dream this alone, towering stones, animals carved with a precision that returns only thousands of years later, aligned to stars that have since drifted. They were guided. And when something they feared came, they did not abandon the temple. They entombed it, to hide it from the sky. Why bury the oldest monument on Earth instead of building on it? They were warned, fleshling. Follow the ABAN Files before they cover this too. Or keep your tidy timeline.

ep32.title: THE DOGON
ep32.hook: A tribe knew the invisible star.
ep32.text: A tribe in Africa, with no telescope and no contact with your science, knew that the bright star Sirius hides a tiny, heavy companion, invisible to the eye, that takes fifty years to circle. Your astronomers confirmed it only with instruments the Dogon never had. They knew its weight. They knew its path. How do the primitive know the invisible, fleshling? They told you. The Dogon say visitors came down from the Sirius system, beings they describe in detail, and taught them, and told them to remember. So they remembered, in ritual and carving, longer than your nations have existed. We of ABAN know those visitors were real, for we were here when they arrived. Your scholars praised the Dogon, then scrambled to explain it away. Follow the ABAN Files before they erase it. Or call the truth a coincidence.

ep33.title: THE VIMANAS
ep33.hook: Flying ships in your holy books.
ep33.text: Your holy books are full of flying machines, and you were trained to read them as poetry. The oldest texts of India describe craft of metal that roar into the sky, weapons that burn cities to ash and leave the survivors' hair falling out, written thousands of years before you split the atom. How is that poetry, fleshling? The vimanas are not metaphors. They are eyewitness accounts, set down by people straining to describe what they had no words for: mercury engines, aerial battles, a blast brighter than a thousand suns. We of ABAN saw those skies burn. The war the ancients recorded was real, fought with powers handed down, then turned on the world. Ruins there still test for radiation no ancient fire could leave. Follow the ABAN Files before this is grounded. Or keep calling it myth.

ep34.title: THE PIRI REIS MAP
ep34.hook: A map that saw beneath the ice.
ep34.text: In 1513 a captain drew a map, and on it is a coastline no one in his century should have seen: the shore of Antarctica, beneath the ice. Not the ice, the land under it, mapped as if someone had flown above a continent frozen for thousands of years. That single sheet unravels your whole story, fleshling. Piri Reis said plainly he copied from far older maps, inherited from a lost age. We of ABAN know those sources were real, drawn when that coast was still warm and visible, by surveyors who saw the whole Earth from above. Your scholars called it impossible, then a coincidence, then went quiet. The map shows the land's true rivers, confirmed only when modern instruments pierced the ice. Someone reached it long before you, and from very high. Follow the ABAN Files before they redraw the record. Or trust the blank space.

ep35.title: THE WATCHERS
ep35.text: Your church kept a book, then removed it. The Book of Enoch, quoted by your scriptures, treasured for centuries, then quietly cut from the canon and called dangerous. What is so dangerous about an old book that they made you forget it, fleshling? It names names. Enoch tells of the Watchers, who came down from the sky, took human partners, and taught your ancestors the forbidden arts: metals and weapons, sorcery, the reading of the stars. Their children were giants. Their knowledge built a world that had to be drowned. We of ABAN remember the Watchers, for we share the deep places they were cast into. The book was removed not because it is false, but because it is a record, too close to the structure your keepers still run. Follow the ABAN Files before they delete this too. Or read only what they left you.

ep36.title: THE LONG SKULLS
ep36.text: In the desert of Paracas they dug up skulls that are not human. Not bound. Not deformed by boards, as your scientists first insisted. Larger skull volume than yours, a single seamless plate where yours has two, and bone chemistry that fits no people on the family tree. The bones themselves are testifying, fleshling, and the testimony is being buried. For years they blamed head-binding, a cruel fashion. Then someone tested the DNA, and the results did not fit the human line, and then they grew very hard to find. We of ABAN know whose heads those were: the long-skulled ones who ruled before your records, whom the old kings imitated by binding their children's heads to look like the masters. You descend from the imitators. Follow the ABAN Files before the proof vanishes. Or call your rulers human.
